newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Bearish India's Jan gas oil purchases expected.
newsitem.headline: Bearish India's Jan gas oil purchases expected.

text.p: Bearish projections of India's gas oil purchases for January, revised down to below 500,000 tonnes, is putting downward pressure on the Singapore gas oil swap market, industry sources said on Friday.
"Results may not be as bullish as expected," said a trader referring to state importer Indian Oil Corp's (IOC) January gas oil tender which closed November 21 and is expected to be awarded Friday.
Sentiment swung around as just on Thursday, traders expected a hefty 700,000-tonnes to be awarded, up from the 520,000-tonnes that was awarded in December.
On Friday morning, brokers and traders said India may only buy as much as 200,000-500,000 tonnes for January.
"I read that as bearish," said a trader who has been selling the December swap.
December gas oil was traded down on Friday morning from $30.51 to $30.43 a barrel. It was last quoted on Thursday at $30.30/$30.40 unchanged, brokers said.
